title: Anthropic IPO: Why I'm Watching (And Why You Should Wait)
creator: Asymmetric Investing
summary: Travis Hoyt of Asymmetric Investing walks through five things to know before buying Anthropic on IPO day. The shares priced at $83 (~$1.4T valuation) and looked set to open near $100 (~$1.5-1.6T), or roughly 25x sales. Growth has been extraordinary - revenue up from $1.4B a year ago (caption figures are garbled in places) - but the growth rate has slowed to about 47% quarter over quarter as competition from OpenAI and Alphabet intensifies and token prices fall. Margins look strong at 86% gross profit, but R&D spending on model training far exceeds cost of sales, so the true cost of serving revenue is rising and margins slipped in Q3. Shareholders get no real say: founders take Class F stock with 50.1% voting power. Finally, Anthropic's cult-like mission is a positive in his view - clear vision beyond money, like early Apple - though others may see it as a risk. His verdict is to wait: IPOs often pop then sink over six months, and the better buying opportunity usually comes 6-24 months later, though Anthropic could join his portfolio in future. He also notes the IPO's transparency will cut both ways for the AI sector: strong Anthropic numbers would support the AI trade, weak ones could spread pessimism to chips, infrastructure and construction names.

calls.video_title: Anthropic IPO: Why I'm Watching (And Why You Should Wait)
calls.thesis: Don't buy on IPO day - wait. IPOs often pop then sink over 6 months; the better buying opportunity usually comes 6-24 months later. At ~$100 expected open (~$1.5-1.6T valuation, ~25x sales) growth is slowing (~47% QoQ) as competition rises and token prices fall, R&D/training spend is eating margins, and founders hold 50.1% voting via Class F so shareholders have no real vote. Anthropic could join his portfolio later.
calls.base_case: Growth slows to 30-40% YoY and the ~25x sales multiple proves too rich.
calls.bull_case: Growth stays near 10x YoY and 25x sales is a fair price; the cult-like mission drives a durable winner.
calls.bear_case: Margins keep falling as training spend rises while revenue growth slows; weak numbers spread pessimism across the whole AI sector.
